title: Edge VPC Configurator & Health Telemetry Terraform Module
creator: Marisa Chen
description: Purpose: Build a reusable Terraform module (edge_vpc_configurator) that provisions opinionated VPC networking for Private deployments with built-in health telemetry and safe upgrade paths. Scope includes AZ-aware subnet tiling, NAT/IGW selection, VPC Endpoint cataloging (S3, Dynamo/SQL, Secrets Manager, KMS-friendly endpoints), route table orchestration, and active health checks and reconciliation webhooks. Goals: 1) Single module can produce public/private/isolated VPC topologies with consistent tagging and guardrails; 2) Automated health probes that detect NAT/IGW egress failures, endpoint reachability issues, and route drift; 3) Safe upgrade/migration plan for in-place Terraform upgrades and rolling replace of NAT gateways across AZs; 4) Strong observability: topology metrics, probe success rates, and degraded-state alerts.
acceptance_criteria: Module publishes outputs: vpc_id, public_subnets, private_subnets, nat_gateway_ids, endpoint_ids, route_table_map
Module supports var.enable_igw | var.enable_nat to toggle egress strategy and documents cost implications
Health check lambda (or operator) runs synthetic egress probes every minute, emits metrics to Datadog/CloudWatch, and creates a Prometheus-friendly endpoint
Terraform plan preserves existing subnet tagging and does not destroy subnets unless explicit var.force_replace=true
Upgrade path validated: can rotate NAT gateways one AZ at a time with zero packet loss observed in synthetic probes
E2E test harness (terragrunt wrapper) deploys to a sandbox account and validates endpoint policies and route reconciliation
design_notes:
- Subnet tiling: use 'subnet_roles' map with deterministic CIDR allocation per AZ to avoid drift.
- Default to NAT gateways in each AZ; support single-shared NAT as an opt-in for cost-sensitive customers.
- Endpoint provisioning will create interface endpoints in private subnets and gateway endpoints for S3 with policy attachment hooks.
- Route table controller: Terraform will create canonical route table resources and register a lightweight reconciliation lambda (pulled into module) that compares live routes vs expected and emits findings.
- Health probes: two-pronged approach: synthetic egress (tcp/https probes to known external endpoints via NAT/IGW) and endpoint reachability checks (TLS handshake + signed request to S3/KMS test objects).
- Upgrade strategy: add lifecycle rules and create_before_destroy patterns for NATs, use tags to coordinate rolling replacement, and document manual failover steps if cross-AZ latency spikes occur.
- Security: endpoints will use least-privileged IAM roles for probes; KMS operations use encrypted env vars; require org-level SSO for module-level admin operations.
implementation_tasks: Define module inputs/outputs and example terragrunt configuration
Implement subnet allocator with deterministic CIDR math and multi-AZ awareness
Implement NAT/IGW toggle logic and create_before_destroy lifecycle for NATs
Create endpoint provisioning with attachable policies and optional cross-account sharing
Build health check lambda/operator (probe runner + route reconciler) and packaging into module
Add Datadog/CloudWatch metric emission and alert rules (produce recommended thresholds)
Add acceptance tests in CI that run in a sandbox account and validate upgrades
Document migration steps and runbook for on-call teams
risks_and_tradeoffs:
- Cost vs availability: per-AZ NAT improves resiliency but increases cost. We will default to per-AZ NAT and provide shared-NAT as opt-in.
- Provider drift: embedding reconciliation lambda increases operational surface area but prevents silent outages from manual route edits.
- Terraform purity vs operator: keeping reconciliation in Terraform (packaged lambda) mixes IaC with runtime behavior; decision: keep operator lightweight and bundled but allow customers to opt out.
- Rollout complexity: automated rotation reduces human error but must be rate-limited to avoid cross-AZ capacity storms. We'll implement a rate limiter with configurable window.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for CIDR allocator and plan-time validation.
- Integration test: terragrunt deploy in sandbox org: validate NAT replacement sequence and health probe metrics remain >99% success.
- Chaos test: simulate IGW failure and validate probes detect failure and promote fallback NAT route if configured.
- Security scan: run tfsec, check IAM least-privilege, and conduct an internal security review before release.
- Smoke test: run post-deploy smoke script to exercise endpoints (S3 put/get, KMS encrypt/decrypt, Secrets Manager get) through provisioned interfaces.
observability_and_alerting:
- Emit metrics: probe_success_rate, route_drift_count, endpoint_latency_ms, nat_replacement_in_progress.
- Create Datadog monitors: probe_success_rate < 95% for 3 mins -> page on-call; route_drift_count > 0 -> create ticket in infra-team queue.
- Traceability: correlate probe failures with recent terraform applies (capture apply id via tag).
rollout_and_migration:
- Beta: enable module for internal private-deploy sandboxes only for 2 weeks.
- Canary upgrade: pick two non-prod customers and run NAT rotation during low-traffic windows verifying synthetic probe SLOs.
- General rollout: after canaries, provide runbook to customers and enable opt-in via feature flag in private deployment UI.
- Backout plan: snapshot route tables and AMI (if any infra changes), and allow immediate reattach of old NATs using preserved allocation IDs.
open_questions: Should reconciliation be implemented as a managed Redwood service or remain bundled in the module?
What is the minimal probe set that satisfies compliance teams for Private deployments?
Do we support cross-account interface endpoints by default or require an explicit opt-in?
